title: Influence of augmented reality-assisted informed consent process on patients’ knowledge, anxiety, and satisfaction in vascular surgery: a randomised, controlled clinical trial
summary:
For planned operations on blood vessels, it is important that patients understand the planned procedure, possible risks, alternative treatment options, and the expected recovery. Conventional counselling is often based on written information and verbal explanations. Providing additional three-dimensional visualizations of body structures and surgical steps may improve patients’ understanding.

This study investigates whether counselling supported by three-dimensional visualization using augmented reality improves patients’ understanding before planned surgery on blood vessels. In addition, the study examines whether this form of counselling affects anxiety related to the operation, patient satisfaction with the counselling, and attitudes toward the use of digital media.

Adult patients receiving counselling before planned surgery on blood vessels are randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group receives the usual counselling with written information and a personal consultation. The other group receives the same information and, in addition, an interactive three-dimensional visualization of the blood vessels and the planned procedure on a tablet device.

Immediately before and after the counselling session, anxiety related to the operation and understanding of the information provided are assessed. After the counselling session, patient satisfaction and attitudes toward the use of digital media are also assessed. Understanding is evaluated both by a questionnaire containing specific knowledge questions and by patients’ self-assessment of their understanding.
conditions: Peripheral vascular diseases in patients scheduled for elective vascular surgery.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients presenting for preoperative counselling before planned vascular surgery who are able to understand the information required for participation in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
Cognitive impairment
Insufficient language proficiency to participate in the counselling process and complete the study assessments
